audit.whatIsWrong: The difficulty rating and the level chart say opposite things. diff is TRICKY at 7/10 with Malzahar carry threat 7.5/10, while the packet chart and win[0..6] both give Akshan all seven rows and the win rate is 51.04% over 1918 games. Separately phases[N].side reads 'Skill' on rows 0,1,2,3,5 and 'Malzahar' on rows 4 and 6 — disagreeing with win[N] on every row.
audit.corrected: diff to EVEN, diffRating 5.5/10, carryRating 6/10, tone to the even colour, and all seven phases[N].side to Akshan matching win[N] and the packet.
audit.why: A 51% win rate with the enemy owning zero stages of the chart cannot also be a 7/10 difficulty. Malzahar's threat is real but it is one 140-second ultimate, not a lane he wins. Bringing the rating to EVEN makes the page agree with its own chart and its own data.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three problems. (1) Call of the Void SILENCES and nothing on the page says so. (2) Void Shift is described only as 'his passive shield'. (3) early and whys[4] and spikes[0] describe Akshan as having a 'dash-refund passive' and 'Heroic Swing's dash'.
audit.why: Call of the Void is 900 range on a flat 6s and it silences — which means it takes Heroic Swing away for its duration. That is the decisive interaction of the matchup: Akshan's only escape can be removed on a six-second cooldown, so pre-casting the swing is how you die here. Void Shift gives massive damage reduction AND crowd control immunity while he has not recently taken damage, so the correct opener is any cheap hit to strip it before committing — 'passive shield' does not tell the reader that. And Akshan has no dash and no cooldown refund from his passive; Heroic Swing is a grappling hook needing terrain.
audit.corrected: Silence written into early, wants.foe[0] and breakdown.cooldowns; Void Shift's damage reduction and CC immunity named with the strip-it-first instruction; the fabricated dash-refund removed from early, spikes[0] and whys[4].
sources: brief enemyKit P/Q text and flags (silence on Q)

audit.why: Nether Grasp is 140s at rank 1 — by far the longest cooldown in the lane and the one worth tracking. Call of the Void is a flat 6s at every rank. Malefic Visions is 11/10/9/8/7.

audit.why: Both packet suspectNames entries are false positives: 'Heroic Swing' is Akshan's real E name, and 'Void Staff' in spikes[3] is a real item, not a garbled 'Void Shift'. Those fields needed changing for other reasons.

notes: The single most important missing fact: Call of the Void silences, on a flat 6-second cooldown at 900 range. Akshan's only escape is Heroic Swing, so a silence deletes his answer — nothing on the page mentioned it, and the whole 'bank the swing' advice elsewhere depends on knowing it can be taken away. Second: Void Shift is CC immunity plus massive damage reduction until he takes damage, so the opener is a cheap hit to strip it; the page called it 'his passive shield', which reads as something to wait out rather than something to break. Third, the same fabricated Akshan mechanic that appears on the Lux page appears here — 'dash-refund passive' and 'Heroic Swing's dash'. Akshan has neither. I flagged this as a champion-level pattern in unverified because it likely recurs across every akshan_mid matchup, not just my slice. I also brought diff/diffRating/carryRating/tone and both difficulty strings from TRICKY 7/10 to EVEN 5.5/10 so the rating stops contradicting a chart that gives Akshan all seven rows at a 51.04% win rate — Medium confidence, since that is a judgement about presentation rather than a kit fact. NOT asserted: the brief's execute-threshold flag on Malefic Visions. Riot's text describes a damage-over-time that spreads to a nearby unit when the target dies — there is no health-threshold execute in the description, so I treated the flag as a parse misfire and wrote nothing about tracking an HP number.
